I was hoping to "move this along", but there wasn't enough sample capture data to be able to update the dissector and make sure I didn't break anything.  I made some minor changes to the existing code, but mostly just rebased and squashed the commits.
Yes the protocol looks to be a big bit packer of data, but I think most developers would find it easier to read if the dissector API used "byte APIs" with bitmasks.
The "sample capture" appears to be taken from another traffic capturing application and then run through text2pcap, where some of the information has been lost (like pinfo->p2p_dir).
I've been in this situation myself with "embedded devices" and traffic capture applications that capture RS-232 devices and use a text based file format.  With that you have 2 options:
1. Make a "custom" text2pcap application that can convert the "raw text bytes" into a pcap, but also provide a few basic pieces of data like timestamps and "direction" (p2p_dir).  We probably wouldn't accept that application into the Wireshark source, so you'd always have the extra "conversion step" before Wireshark could read the data using the provided dissector.
2. Add a wiretap for the file format.  This allows Wireshark to more "natively" read the capture file and can internally provide things like p2p_dir and any other "hints" the dissector would need that isn't "raw packet data".  There are several "text based" wiretaps, mostly coming from CAN based capturing tools and I think you could model a dcc-rail wiretap after those.
Providing a much bigger sample capture and official links to the spec(s) would allow other developers (like me) to potentially work on this.
